transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Yeah, hey, thanks for fitting me in. So, the reason I made the appointment... well, it’s mostly because of work. I’m a firefighter, which, you know, is a job where you gotta be ready to go from zero to sixty in a second. And I’m good at that part. But the problem is... I feel like I’m always running hot. Like, constantly. It’s like I have this internal motor running inside me and I just can’t shut it off, no matter how hard I try. 

Even when we get back from a brutal call at 3 AM and all the other guys crash in the bunks, I'm still just vibrating, pacing the bay, wiping down the engine for the third time, you know? And lately, that’s been getting me in trouble at the firehouse. My captain actually pulled me aside because I guess I'm driving the rest of the crew nuts. They're trying to decompress or watch a movie, and I'm just constantly up and down, messing with stuff, pacing around the kitchen... I just can't power down. It's like the engine is just stuck on high idle all day and all night, and my lieutenant was basically like, "You need to get this figured out because you're exhausting everyone else." So, yeah, that's why I'm here.
Along with this constant physical restlessness, do you also find yourself worrying a lot or having racing anxious thoughts that you can't control?

No, no, it’s not really like that. I wouldn't say I'm worried. I mean, people always assume that, right? They see me pacing a hole in the floor at the station and they’re like, "Man, what’s eating you? What are you stressing about?" But I'm honestly not stressing at all. My brain isn't stuck on, you know, bad thoughts or panicking about the future or anything like that. 

Like, even after a really intense call—say we go out to a bad structure fire or a messy car wreck on the interstate—some of the guys will come back and they’re definitely in their heads about it. They're processing, maybe they're a little anxious or rattled. But me? I’m not replaying the scary parts, I’m not worrying about what could have gone wrong or what’s gonna happen on the next shift. My mind is actually just... well, it's bouncing around, sure, but not with worry. It’s more like, "I should check the oil on the K-12 saw," and then two seconds later, "I wonder if someone ate the rest of the chili," and then, "I really need to fix that squeaky hinge on the locker room door." 

So it’s not this heavy, anxious dread or racing panic. I'm not sitting there chewing my nails because I'm scared. It’s purely just this physical need to be doing something, moving around, fixing something, touching something. The thoughts aren't anxious, they just kind of... match the physical energy, if that makes sense. I just need to be in motion. So, yeah, no, I wouldn't say I'm a worrier at all.

Thinking back, did you notice this same kind of restlessness and constant need to be moving or doing something back when you were a kid or in school, or is this something that really only started as an adult?

Oh, man, no, this is definitely not a new thing. Not at all. If you ask my mom, she’d probably laugh and say I’ve been this way since I learned to walk. Actually, we were just talking about this the other day when I went over to her house to help her clean out her garage—which, by the way, was an absolute disaster, but I really needed a project to do on my day off to keep myself busy—and she was saying how I was exactly like this back in grade school. 

Like, second, third grade, all the way up through middle school. She said she used to absolutely dread parent-teacher conferences because the teachers would always, without fail, say the exact same thing. I was always, always out of my seat. Like, I’d get up to sharpen my pencil five times during a twenty-minute math lesson, or I'd just be wandering around the back of the classroom looking at the terrarium or the bulletin boards while the teacher was trying to give a lesson. 

And the blurting out! Man, if I knew the answer, or honestly even if I just had a random thought pop into my head about whatever we were talking about, I just couldn't hold it in. I'd just yell it out before anyone else could even raise their hand. It drove my teachers crazy. And then there was the homework... I mean, I’d do it, sometimes, but it would never make it from my backpack to the teacher's desk. My backpack was just a black hole of crumpled papers and missing assignments. 

So my mom was constantly getting notes sent home, getting phone calls from the principal's office... and the frustrating part for her, and for the teachers I guess, was that they all knew I was bright enough to do the work. Like, the concepts weren't too hard for me at all. I could ace the tests if I actually sat still long enough to take them, but the sitting still and the keeping track of my papers? It was just a total disaster. So, yeah, this whole motor-running, can't-stop-moving thing? It’s been with me pretty much my whole life, not just since I became an adult or joined the fire department. It just looks a little different now, I guess, but the core of it... yeah, exact same thing back then.
